tier_reason: The auto-generated Flux README gives per-model first-gradient and warm-gradient times for Mooncake vs Zygote on CPU and GPU. The harness is public (test/integration_testing/flux/benchmarks.jl: median of at least 10 samples within a 2-second budget, fresh process for first-gradient runs), the toolchain is stated (Julia 1.12.7 JIT, 1 thread, exact run command; Julia takes no compiler flags) and the hardware is named (Cortex-X925 + Cortex-A725 CPU, NVIDIA GB10).

corrections.stars_or_usage: 409 stars, 38 forks; main README: 'On one system, Flux benchmarks found Mooncake gradient evaluations after warm-up were 2.03 times as fast as Zygote on CPU across 19 models, with comparable GPU performance.'
corrections.caveats: Single system (Arm GB10 machine: Cortex-X925 + Cortex-A725, NVIDIA GB10) and tiny Flux layers enlarged 32x. Several warm CPU rows are slower than Zygote (LayerNorm(2) 1.38x, MultiHeadAttention(16) 1.37x, Flux.Scale 1.26x, SkipConnection 1.03x). On GPU the warm gain is only 1.05x by geometric mean, and several layers are slower. First gradient is much slower (geometric-mean ratio 10.57 on CPU, 3.26 on GPU; for example Dense(2 => 4) 12.5 s vs 693 ms) because Mooncake's measurement includes prepare_gradient_cache. The recorded revision is 'ed99f98b0-dirty' (benchmarks.jl marks any git status output as dirty, so the run may include uncommitted changes). Baseline is Zygote.jl, not oneDNN/cuDNN/XNNPACK/Eigen. Julia library, not callable from C++.

notes: All quoted numbers verified in the Flux README (2.03x CPU warm, 0.493 and 10.57 CPU ratios, 0.952 and 3.26 GPU ratios, LSTM 4.04 ms vs 1.75 ms, RNN 1.62 ms vs 313 us); benchmarks.jl opened. Metadata matches: MIT, 409 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-30. Scope: Julia-only; keep as a non-C++ entry or flag for the language filter.

tier_reason: The README's speed figure is Figure 4 of the QRNN paper (arXiv 1611.01576, Nov 2016), which predates this repository's first commit ('QRNN Release', 2017-09-28); a WebSearch summary says the paper's experiments used a Chainer implementation, so no peer-reviewed number was measured on this code. The only numbers for this PyTorch code are first-party: the awd-lstm-lm README gives per-epoch times on an NVIDIA Quadro GP100 without PyTorch, CUDA or cuDNN versions.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README text: 'betwen 2 and 17 times faster than the highly optimized NVIDIA cuDNN LSTM implementation depending on the use case'; repo description: 'up to 16 times faster'. The reproduced paper figure (Figure 4, measured on the paper's earlier implementation) shows inference speed advantages over cuDNN LSTM from 1.3x (batch 256) to 16.9x (batch 8, sequence length 512), and training on a two-layer 640-unit PTB LM of roughly 290 ms/batch for the cuDNN LSTM vs roughly 150 ms/batch for the QRNN (read off the bar chart). Numbers measured with this PyTorch code (awd-lstm-lm README, NVIDIA Quadro GP100): Penn Treebank LSTM 65 s/epoch vs QRNN 28 s/epoch, WikiText-2 180 vs 90 s/epoch (about 2.3x and 2.0x, derived from page data).
corrections.hardware: NVIDIA Quadro GP100 for the awd-lstm-lm per-epoch times; GPU for the paper figure not stated on the pages opened
corrections.caveats: The README's 2-17x figure is Figure 4 of the ICLR 2017 paper, measured before this PyTorch code existed (by a WebSearch summary, on a Chainer implementation); the figure itself starts at 1.3x, not 2x, at batch size 256. Numbers measured on this code come only from the sibling awd-lstm-lm README (about 2x per epoch on a Quadro GP100) with no PyTorch, CUDA or cuDNN versions, and the QRNN and LSTM models there differ in depth and width. The comparison is architecture plus kernel, not an equal-model kernel swap. CUDA kernels are compiled at runtime via CuPy and pynvrtc against 2017-era PyTorch (Variable API); the repository is archived (2022-02-12) and its last code commit is 2017-11-26. Old cuDNN (2016-2017 era); modern cuDNN LSTM is faster.

notes: Downgraded B to C: the peer-reviewed numbers belong to the paper's earlier implementation, and this repository has only first-party per-epoch timings (via awd-lstm-lm). The low end of the README claim is overstated (the figure shows 1.3x at batch 256). Metadata matches: BSD-3-Clause, 1.3k stars, archived 2022-02-12.
